works.abstract: Microplastics have become a pervasive pollutant in the environment, the extent to which is now being studied. A good initial step to understand how they are impacting the environment is to engage in testing/monitoring programs for the analysis of water to detect and characterize microplastics. Unfortunately, these analyses can be very complex, requiring significant expertise for the operation of intricate instrumentation. This presentation will introduce and discuss a new, automated approach, utilizing laser-based molecular microspectroscopy, to simplify the characterization of microplastics.
works.journal: Illinois Digital Environment for Access to Learning and Scholarship (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign)
works.title: Automated Characterization of Microplastics Using a Laser-based Analyzer

works.abstract: Interest in investigating microplastics in the environment has been increasing rapidly in recent years. The focus of recent research efforts is to understand the environmental impacts of the ubiquitous presence of microplastics. Plastics never fully degrade; larger plastic waste eventually breaks down into smaller particles. Even relatively inert polymers, e.g., polyethylene, can function as vectors for various pollutants. The preferred technique for measuring microplastics is vibrational spectroscopy, and the most common vibrational spectroscopic technique is infrared (IR). The advantages include chemical specificity, many libraries exist for identifying measured spectra, it is non-destructive, and it can be highly automated. Accurate identification of microplastics requires, in addition to an IR spectrometer, a microscope to see the extremely small particles and to set up scanning parameters. Unfortunately, the analysis can be complicated and often requires significant skill in microscopic measurement techniques. To that end, an automated quantum cascade laser-based infrared analyzer has been developed for the fast, accurate analysis of microplastics that can be used by users of all skill levels. This presentation will describe the analyzer and will show that, using the analyzer’s microplastics workflow, microplastics can be easily characterized.

works.title: Automated Analysis Microplastics Using a Quantum Cascade-based Infrared Analyzer
